recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR source change is needed for FHIR-18492; future changes to narrative safety or image rules should be handled as separate narrative-page or XHTML-content decisions rather than by reverting the Narrative root definition.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive FHIR-core narrative issue raised against STU3 requesting replacement of the old Narrative definition, "A human-readable formatted text, including images", with a human-readable summary definition conveying the essential clinical and business information for the resource, with image allowance moved to comments.
initial_application: The Jira comment cites GH#9cad63bc63. Commit 9cad63bc639139c7a04b8c84407de26df7654128 changed source/datatypes/narrative.xml by replacing the Narrative short description and formal definition with the accepted summary/essential-clinical-and-business wording. The existing Narrative.div comment already described XHTML image allowance.
additional_context: Narrative remains active current-build source: source/fhir.ini lists Narrative as infrastructure, maps narrative/xhtml to narrative.html, marks Narrative normative, and assigns the txt abbreviation. Current narrative guidance says non-empty narrative SHALL reflect all content needed for a human to understand the essential clinical and business information. Generated CI output displays the accepted Narrative definition and the Narrative.div image comment. Earlier FHIR-9826 and later FHIR-17463 support the same narrative-safety direction and do not supersede the FHIR-18492 definition.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit was made because the authoritative source and generated CI output already satisfy the accepted Jira request.
